collection_notes: Harvested outlet RSS/atom + news-sitemaps (variety, hollywoodreporter, deadline, indiewire, nofilmschool, fxguide, beforesandafters, provideocoalition, cartoonbrew, vfxvoice, postperspective, theasc, motionographer, studiodaily, animationmagazine, awn, redsharknews, 80.lv) plus AI tag feeds and YouTube channel feeds (fxguide, Curious Refuge, Matt Wolfe). 2 WebSearch queries used to fill Runway/Sora and festival gaps. Every published time taken from og article:published_time / JSON-LD datePublished / RSS pubDate / sitemap news:publication_date, then gated with freshness.py (movies=336h). Dropped as non-AI or off-beat: Strada + QScan IBC updates (no AI content), Disney CTO appointment (exec move), WarGames rewatch essay, Apple Siri / AI data-center items from The Verge & Engadget (no film hook). Per-outlet cap 3 enforced; 12 distinct outlets.

items.headline: Tom Cruise Says AI Is 'Coming and It's Going to Happen,' but 'People Want to See Real Things'
items.excerpt: Accepting a BAFTA fellowship, Tom Cruise delivered a six-minute defense of human-made cinema, conceding AI is inevitable in production but arguing audiences still come for real stunts, real faces and real craft.

items.headline: Tom Cruise Earns Applause With Six-Minute Monologue On Why Art Beats AI In Filmmaking
items.excerpt: Deadline's account of the same BAFTA speech focuses on Cruise's craft argument: that the physical, analog labor of filmmaking is precisely what generative tools cannot substitute for.

items.headline: The Old & New Hollywood Guard Wielding AI's Might
items.excerpt: Variety maps 10 companies — from Runway and Higgsfield to Particle 6 and legacy VFX houses — by the specific production use case each has staked out, a rare side-by-side of who does previs, relighting, de-aging and full generation.

items.headline: Duncan Jones on Why It's 'Harder Than Ever' to Make His Kind of Movies (and Why He Refused to Use AI)
items.excerpt: Duncan Jones explains the production-economics squeeze on mid-budget genre films and why he deliberately kept generative AI out of his new feature despite the budget pressure that would have justified it.

items.headline: AI Actor Tilly Norwood Glitches During Piers Morgan Interview, Suddenly Switches Languages
items.excerpt: The synthetic performer marketed as a bookable actor broke character mid-interview and switched languages, a live demonstration of how far real-time AI talent still sits from performance reliability.

items.headline: After Effects AI Assistant enters public beta
items.excerpt: Adobe's conversational assistant for After Effects opened to public beta at IBC2026, letting compositors describe an effect or a fix in plain language and have the app build the layer and expression setup.

items.headline: Beeble SwitchX 2.0: native 4K, 20-second clips and a Reframe outpainting tool
items.excerpt: Beeble's AI relighting and background-replacement tool for filmmakers moves to native 4K, 20-second clips and 10-bit color, and adds Reframe — an outpainting pass that changes a shot's aspect ratio without a reshoot.

items.headline: Adobe Unveils Photoshop Elements and Premiere Elements 2027 With New AI-Powered Capabilities
items.excerpt: Adobe pushes its consumer-tier editors to a 2027 release built around AI-assisted cutting, cleanup and color, pulling pro-grade automation down into the entry-level filmmaking tier.

items.headline: You Don't Have to Use AI in Your Film, But Can You Prove You Didn't?
items.excerpt: A practical look at creative provenance: as festivals and buyers start demanding AI disclosure, filmmakers who abstained now need a verifiable paper trail through their own pipeline to prove it.

items.headline: More AI Editing Assistance is on the Way as Eddie AI V4 is Unveiled Ahead of IBC 2026
items.excerpt: Eddie AI's fourth version deepens the assistant-editor role — logging, selects and rough assembly — aiming at the unglamorous prep hours rather than the creative cut itself.

items.headline: IBC 2026: Splats, Sync and Scene-Aware Cameras
items.excerpt: A show-floor read on where production tech landed at IBC: Gaussian splat capture moving into mainstream post pipelines, AI-driven sync and metadata, and cameras that understand the scene they are recording.

items.headline: Jim Cameron's Lightstorm Vision Buys Outsyders for 3D AI Pipeline
items.excerpt: Cameron's Lightstorm Vision absorbs 3D conversion house Outsyders to build an in-house AI-assisted stereo conversion pipeline, folding a vendor service into the studio's own toolchain.

items.headline: Origami Platform Updates MAM, Audio Conform, Security and AI Capabilities
items.excerpt: Origami's media-management release adds AI-driven search and audio conform, targeting the archive-and-retrieval layer where post teams lose the most time.

items.headline: VFX supervisor Eran Dinur discusses the big AI and ML changes that have impacted visual effects
items.excerpt: A working VFX supervisor walks through which parts of the effects pipeline machine learning actually changed — roto, cleanup, denoise — and which parts stubbornly still require artists.

items.headline: Pitch Black's Troy Tobin on where Rising Sun's REVIZE is now headed
items.excerpt: Rising Sun Pictures' REVIZE face-work toolset gets a roadmap update from Pitch Black's Troy Tobin, covering how the ML-driven likeness pipeline is being productized for other studios.

items.headline: Battle of the NLE AI Assistants
items.excerpt: Scott Simmons runs Adobe's Premiere assistant against DaVinci Resolve's on real timeline tasks, a hands-on comparison of whether either assistant survives contact with an actual edit.

items.headline: Insta360 X6 turns 360 video into explorable 3D scenes
items.excerpt: Insta360's Spatial Capture feature turns ordinary 360 footage into 3D Gaussian splats, pushing neural scene capture down to a consumer camera that location scouts and previs teams already carry.

items.headline: Blackmagic Design Updates DaVinci Resolve
items.excerpt: DaVinci Resolve 21.1 adds AI-assistant integration alongside expanded camera-format support, putting a conversational layer on top of the grade and edit page.

items.headline: Murphy Pre-Prod Software Applies New Tech to Film Planning, Not Generation
items.excerpt: Murphy positions itself against generative tools by applying AI to scheduling, breakdowns and previs logistics — the planning layer — rather than to image making.

items.headline: 2D AI worlds breaking camera tracking
items.excerpt: fxguide explains the concrete failure mode when 2D generative world models meet a real VFX pipeline: there is no consistent 3D geometry underneath, so camera tracking and matchmove fall apart.

items.headline: Why a Gaussian 'splat' helps lighting — go 3D+2D, not all-3D
items.excerpt: A short argument for hybrid pipelines: using Gaussian splats as a lighting and environment layer alongside traditional 3D rather than trying to rebuild the whole shot in geometry.

items.headline: Camera Angles Are Becoming a Thing of the Past
items.excerpt: Curious Refuge argues that as generative video lets you re-angle a scene after the fact, shot selection stops being a set decision and becomes a post decision — a real change to how coverage is planned.
